title: Remove the smallest
prompt: heap is a valid min-heap stored in an array. Remove its smallest value and return it, leaving a valid min-heap. Return undefined for an empty heap. Move the last element to the root and sift it down, always swapping with the smaller child.
hints: After the root is taken, which element fills the hole, and why that one?
The last element keeps the tree free of gaps. From the root, compare it with its children and swap with the smaller child while that child is smaller.
Find the index of the smallest among the node and its children that exist. Stop when it is the node itself. Take care when the heap has one element.
checks: (() => { const heap = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]; const out: number[] = []; for (let count = 0; count < 7; count++) out.push(heapPop(heap) ?? -1); return __same(out, [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]); })()
(() => { const heap = [1, 5, 2, 9, 6, 3, 8]; const out: number[] = []; for (let count = 0; count < 7; count++) out.push(heapPop(heap) ?? -1); return __same(out, [1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 8, 9]); })()
checkLabels: Removing the only element leaves an empty heap.
Seven removals give the values in order.
Removals from another heap also come out in order.

wrongAnswers.misconception: Always compares with the left child and never looks at the right one.
Puts the last element back at the root even when it was the only one.

feedback: Do the first check by hand on paper, as a tree. After the last element moves to the root, which child is smaller?
